title: DID WE MAKE IT?
version: 2.1 (2026-11-04, Sky: tighten 0:15-1:35 for attention; less lag on T11)
source_of_truth: Words: this file, exactly. Direction and picture: SCRIPT_V2.md. Timing: measured from recordings. start(line) = end(previous line) + gap_before_s; length = measured duration of voices/<id>.wav (leading/trailing silence trimmed to 0.1 s).

speakers.FY: First-year Sky, screen left, leans forward, faster and brighter
speakers.TY: Third-year Sky, screen right, leans back, slower and drier; leans into the lamp only from T17

shots.PAPER: top-down insert of the sheet (memories are drawn here)

preroll.note: NO black opening. Frame 1 = phone face-up on the dark desk, screen glowing (only light in the room). Fan and distant traffic already present.

beat_rule: Lines with 'parts' are generated as separate clips (voices/<ID>_p1.wav, _p2.wav ...) and joined with exactly beat_s of silence. Subtitles use the full 'text'.

lines.speaker: FY
lines.text: Okay, okay — new idea. Hear me out. Um… no, wait. This one's actually big.
lines.delivery: raw, fast, stumbling; a real late-night voice note
lines.insert: phone screen shows a voice-note waveform playing
lines.note: optionally recorded raw by Sky instead of cloned

lines.speaker: FY
lines.insert: FIRST LAUGH: FY flips it, flips it back, then holds it up to the lamp as if there's hidden writing. Nothing. Then the line.

lines.speaker: FY
lines.text: We don't write things down. We talk. Voice notes, all day, every idea. What happened to that guy?
lines.delivery: teasing, familiar; slows on the last sentence
lines.insert: faint waveform flickers over the sheet, dies on 'that guy'

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: I don't know how it ends yet.
lines.delivery: eyes on the page; breath before; first crack

lines.speaker: FY
lines.text: Then don't write it. Say it.

lines.speaker: FY
lines.note: gap covers the title: cut to W, 'DID WE MAKE IT?' fades in small in the lower third for 1.5 s, then out; fan only

lines.speaker: TY
lines.delivery: dry, hint of a smile; laugh line

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Friends were throwing around a hackathon idea. I shipped it in four, five hours.

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Two, three days later I'd bought a domain — didn't even know how domains worked.
lines.delivery: quietly proud; a smile at himself
lines.insert: after the cut: pencil laptop, then a page goes live, then a 'www.' box ticks (generic, no brands)

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Wrong customers. Small sites didn't feel the pain. Big ones already had someone.
lines.insert: sketch splits into small-site vs big-site silhouettes; small rust X at the split

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Spending limits for AI apps. Nobody cared about the bill yet.

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Safety rules for AI agents. Five months. Best thing I've ever built.
lines.delivery: warmest so far; he loved this one
lines.insert: card 'AGENT SAFETY · 5 MONTHS'; small codebase surrounded by gates

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: I was up till three. Every night. Code, customers, emails.
lines.insert: drawn clock, hands sweep from 12 to 3

lines.speaker: TY
lines.sound_after: near-silence (room tone ducked) until Y12 (shortened, Sky 2.1)

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Reddit. One post blew up in a few hours. Mods took it down. Account too new.
parts: Reddit. One post blew up in a few hours.
Mods took it down. Account too new.
lines.insert: generic post card, a line rising, then a flat grey 'REMOVED' stamp (no real UI, no logos, no view counts)

lines.speaker: FY
lines.delivery: a breath of a laugh, on his side

lines.speaker: FY
lines.delivery: quiet; the question he was scared to ask

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: I'd promised myself five thousand dollars a month. By December.
lines.insert: handwritten '$5K / MONTH BY DEC?' then crossed out by hand (an old target, not revenue)

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Applied to YC's first Bengaluru event. 'Seats are full.'

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Placements are next July. Half of me is preparing for that. Half of me is here. Never all in.
lines.insert: a line down the middle of the sheet: 'PLACEMENTS · JULY' on one side, the product sketches on the other

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: So two months ago, I stopped. Everything.
lines.insert_props: three plain book spines on the desk: Zero to One / The Hard Thing About Hard Things / The Lean Startup (titles only, no cover art)

lines.speaker: FY
lines.text: Was I wrong? To want it that big?
lines.delivery: looks at his hands first, then up; not melodramatic
lines.pose: looking down at hands, then up

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: No. You're the only reason I started. You just didn't know how long the middle is.
parts: You're the only reason I started. You just didn't know how long the middle is.
lines.delivery: the centre of the film; warm
lines.pose: leans forward into the lamp (first time)
lines.music: START: original sparse piano motif on 'No.'

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: I kept asking AI for ideas. But real problems don't come from prompts. They come from people. And I've been doing it all alone, in one room.
lines.insert: a prompt box gets crossed out, then small figures of people talking (no identifiable faces)

lines.speaker: TY
lines.text: Get out of this room. Talk to people. Maybe physical AI. Honestly, I don't know yet.
lines.insert: brief flash on PAPER: unfinished pencil sketch of a sensor / robot arm (construction lines visible)

lines.speaker: FY
lines.delivery: certain, the way only a first-year can be

text: A film by Sky · written out loud
end_card.optional_line_only_if_true: Every line and every build prompt was spoken, not typed — with Wispr Flow.

rules: Never paraphrase a line. If a line cannot work, stop and report it.
No logos, no real app UIs, no brand look-alikes. 'Wispr Flow' and 'YC' as plain text only.
No invented customers, revenue, view counts or events.
Physical AI is an exploration, never shown as a built product.
No copyrighted music; the motif is original.
